# SHABM — Menu Engineering, Recipe Costing & Pricing Strategy

## 0. METHOD NOTE — READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING ANY NUMBER

**This session had zero live web access.** The WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200 calls) by earlier agents before this task started, and the organisation's egress proxy returned policy denials (403 on CONNECT) for **every** domain attempted — numbeo.com, ico.org, wikipedia.org, talabat.com, starbucks.com, hungerstation.com, zomato.com, elmenus.com, carrefouruae.com and others. Proxy status confirmed via `curl "$HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status"`. Per `/root/.ccr/README.md` these are policy denials to be reported, not routed around.

**I therefore could not fetch a single new competitor menu price this session.** What I did instead:

1. Mined the **eight prior research files on disk** (`/home/user/AboStesha-claude/shabm/research/*.json`), which were produced by sibling agents in this same project *while web search was still available*. Their citations are real and are carried forward here with attribution intact and their original confidence grades.
2. Rebuilt every recipe **bottom-up from those sourced input prices**, showing the gram/ml arithmetic, so an investor can audit the derivation even where the input itself is an estimate.
3. Ran original quantitative analysis (contribution-per-bottleneck-minute, resource-constrained throughput, Erlang-C queueing, daypart modelling, sensitivity) against the project's own financial model at `/home/user/AboStesha-claude/shabm/financials/`.

**Grading used throughout:**
- **[H]** hard-sourced — a named publication/URL and year, carried from the repo research files
- **[H/E]** hard inputs, my arithmetic on top
- **[E]** my estimate, derivation shown
- **[UNSOURCED-BENCH]** practitioner benchmark from my knowledge base, **not verified this session** — flagged every time

**The single biggest credibility gap in this dimension:** every competitor menu price benchmark (Half Million, Barn's, Dose, %Arabica, Starbucks, Cilantro, Ridha Alwan, Kahvi) that the brief asked for is **either second-hand through the repo's assumptions file or absent**. Section 3.6 lists exactly what must be photographed before this goes in front of an investor.

**Base case used in all pricing below: USD 0.90.** At the Baghdad price of IQD 8,000 (USD 5.23) that is a **82.8% gross margin / 17.2% food cost**.

> ### ⚠ FINDING 1 — the packaging tooling trap (the one real COGS risk on this item)
> The $0.19 cup above assumes a **stock** clear double-wall PET cup with a printed wrap. A genuinely *custom-moulded faceted* vessel — which is what the brand renders show — requires injection-mould tooling at **USD 12,000–25,000**, with typical MOQs of 50,000–100,000 units.
>
> One Baghdad flagship sells ~110 Saqee'/day = **40,150 cups/year**. That is below every MOQ.
>
> | Tooling | Amortised over 50k | over 100k | over 250k |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | $12,000 | +$0.240/cup → COGS $1.14, GM 78.2% | +$0.120 → $1.02, GM 80.5% | +$0.048 → $0.95, GM 81.9% |
> | $18,000 | +$0.360 → $1.26, GM 75.9% | +$0.180 → $1.08, GM 79.3% | +$0.072 → $0.97, GM 81.4% |
> | $25,000 | +$0.500 → $1.40, GM 73.2% | +$0.250 → $1.15, GM 78.0% | +$0.100 → $1.00, GM 80.9% |
>
> **Recommendation:** Year 1 uses a stock double-wall PET cup + a heavily branded printed wrap. Custom tooling only becomes accretive at ~250k cups/year ≈ **8–10 units ≈ Year 3**. Budget the tooling as a **network capex line in Year 3**, not as a Year-1 unit COGS. If the deck shows a custom vessel in Year 1 renders, the COGS line must carry +$0.24–0.50 and GM falls to 73–78%.

> ### ⚠ FINDING 2 — the ULT freezer cannot be a service point
> Repo research 04 establishes: commercial ULT (−80 °C) freezers are rated to a **maximum 30–32 °C ambient** (Thermo TSX 15–32, Eppendorf CryoCube 16–32, Haier DW-86L 10–32, PHCbi MDF-DU 5–30). **Baghdad back-of-house runs 38–45 °C — 6–15 °C above spec.** Separately, a ULT rejects 0.7–1.5 kW continuously into the room (up to 2.5 kW on pull-down).
>
> At the July peak the flagship sells **~24 Saqee'/hour**. Serving direct from the ULT means a door opening **every 2.5 minutes**. No ULT holds −80 °C under that duty cycle; recovery from a single door opening is minutes.
>
> **Operational fix (must be in the deck, and it is a COGS line):** the ULT lives in a **conditioned back-of-house room** (part of the 5–6 TR cooling load already engineered in research 04) and cups are **batch-transferred** — 20–25 at a time, once per hour — into an insulated **−50/−60 °C holding well at the bar**. This is why the $0.063 energy allocation should be held at the model's **$0.10**: batch transfer plus a second holding freezer roughly doubles the per-cup energy. **Keep the model's number.**

**Sensitivity — coffee price is not the risk:**

| Landed coffee | 18 g shot | Saqee' COGS | GM at $5.23 |
|---|---|---|---|
| $14/kg | $0.252 | $0.83 | 84.2% |
| $18/kg | $0.324 | $0.90 | 82.8% |
| $22/kg | $0.396 | $0.97 | 81.4% |

The full sourced band moves gross margin by **2.8 pp**. Packaging moves it by **9.6 pp**. Investor attention should go to packaging, not coffee.

## 1.2 (b) Al-Qalab — iced coffee/tea in a hand-carved clear ice vessel

| Component | Derivation | Cost USD | Grade |
|---|---|---|---|

| **Directional-freeze energy** | Clinebell CB300X2: 272 kg per 3.75-day cycle, ~2.5 kW continuous (circulation pump runs the whole cycle) = 225 kWh ÷ 272 kg = **0.83 kWh/kg**; × 2.0 kg × $0.175 | 0.290 | **[H/E]** |

The real cost is that directional freezing runs a pump and a plate for **3.75 days** to expel dissolved air and get optical clarity. Anyone modelling clear ice off latent heat alone will understate it by ~85%.

**Model carries $2.35** — it prices the vessel at **$1.20** rather than my $0.63. **Both are correct, for different entities:**
- **$0.63** is the *marginal in-house production cost* at a company store with its own Clinebell.
- **$1.20+** is the *transfer price a franchisee pays*, because repo research 08 recommends centralising clear-ice production in each city's lead Cube and selling blocks into the network (this removes **$24,000–27,600** of capex per franchised unit and lifts the franchisor take by **~1.47 pp of AUV**).

**Recommendation: publish both.** Company-store COGS $1.56–1.96; franchisee COGS $2.35. This is a *feature* of the franchise model, not an inconsistency — say so explicitly.

**Base case used below: USD 1.96.** At IQD 15,000 (USD 9.80) = **80.0% GM / 20.0% food cost.**

**Price anchor [H]:** Café 33 (Hyatt Regency Kyoto) and Nishimura Coffee Kobe charge **¥2,000 ≈ USD 13** for this exact format. Baghdad is priced **25% below the Japanese original** — a defensible position for the deck.

> ### ⚠ FINDING 3 — Al-Qalab is supply-constrained, not labour-constrained
> Carving consumes only **0.25 station-equivalents** at a 60-transaction hour. The binding constraint is **block production**:
>
> | Scenario | Al-Qalab/day | vs 1× Clinebell CB300X2 (30–42/day) |
> |---|---|---|
> | Baghdad flagship, mature (300 tx/day) | 21.2 | 59% of one machine |
> | Baghdad flagship, **July peak** (440 tx/day) | **31.1** | **86% — no redundancy** |
> | Rollout Cube, mature (268 tx/day) | 18.9 | 53% |
>
> One machine, a **3.75-day production lead time**, and no OEM service agent in Iraq. A compressor failure closes the hero SKU for weeks. Repo research 04 recommends an **8–12% spares reserve**; the repo `ops.spares_pct` is set to 10%. **Specify a second CB300X2 (or an equivalent) before the flagship opens** — at $16,000–24,000 landed it is cheap insurance on a 12% revenue line, and it converts a fragile hero into a scalable one.

But it must be **mix-capped at peak**, not promoted at peak. See §4.4.

# 2. THE MENU-ENGINEERING CORE: CONTRIBUTION PER BOTTLENECK-MINUTE

## 2.1 The ranking that should drive every menu decision

GM% is the wrong optimisation target for a capacity-constrained kiosk. The right one is **gross profit per minute of the constraining resource.**

# 7. DAYPART STRATEGY

## 7.1 The climate and social facts that decide this

- **Baghdad averages 45 °C in July and August; ~134 days/year above 40 °C** (repo research, Weather Spark).
- **12:00–16:00 in summer is not a trading window — it is a survival window.** The daypart model puts 14:00 at **1.7% of daily transactions**.
- The evening is the primary social occasion. **21:00 is the peak hour at 15.0% of daily volume — 2.10× the flat-day average.**
- **65% of Iraqi transactions are cash** (repo `markets.iraq.card_share = 0.35`) — a late-night cash operation needs a defined drop and reconciliation protocol.

## 7.2 Recommended trading hours

| Season | Hours | Length | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Summer (May–Sep)** | **16:00 – 02:00** | **10 h** | Opening at 12:00 buys 5.9% of volume across 4 hours at 45 °C, while running the full 15.4 kW cooling load and a full staff roster. **Do not open before 16:00 in July and August.** |
| **Shoulder (Apr, Oct)** | 14:00 – 01:00 | 11 h | |
| **Winter (Nov–Mar)** | 10:00 – 00:00 | 14 h | Morning Kahraman trade becomes viable; winter afternoons are the pleasant hours |
| **Ramadan** | **19:00 – 03:00** | 8 h | Inverted day; iftar → suhoor. Worth ~+1.9% annual revenue per unit |
| **Thu/Fri (weekend)** | +1 h close | | Iraqi weekend is Fri–Sat; Thursday night is the peak social night |

> ### ⚠ FINDING 9 — the model assumes a 15-hour summer day; it should assume 10
> The repo's `_util_note` describes a 15-hour trading day and `peak_equivalent_hours` is 8.0–8.5. The daypart analysis says **12:00–16:00 contributes 5.9% of daily transactions** while carrying the **highest cooling load of the day** (peak solar gain is **32% of the 15.4 kW total load** — 20 m² of sunlit glazing × 700 W/m² × SHGC 0.35, per research 04).
>
> **Closing 12:00–16:00 in Jun–Aug:**
> - forgoes ~5.9% of summer transactions ≈ **−1.9% of annual revenue**
> - saves ~4 h/day × ~15 kW × $0.175 = **~$10.50/day of cooling** × 92 days = **~$966**
> - saves ~4 staff-hours/day × 92 days × ~$1.79 = **~$659**
> - **and materially reduces the risk of a ULT or ice-plant thermal failure at the hottest hours of the day** — which is the real prize, since a ULT failure closes 25% of revenue for weeks
>
> Net revenue effect is roughly a wash; **risk effect is strongly positive.** The 8.0–8.5 `peak_equivalent_hours` already in the model is the correct demand ceiling — **but the deck should stop describing a 15-hour day.** Describe a **10-hour evening-concentrated summer day**, which is also a far more credible operating picture to a Gulf F&B investor.

open_questions: BLOCKING FOR THE DECK — not one competitor menu price in this report was obtained first-hand. Is the specialty roasted coffee landed cost really USD 14-22/kg in Baghdad? This is a derived estimate (green USD 11.20-11.70/kg + freight/duty + roast loss + roaster margin), not a quote, and it is the largest single ingredient input in the model. Get three quotes from Baghdad roasters and from Turkish/UAE exporters. Note the sourced Iraqi commodity wholesale price is only USD 2.33-5.77/kg — SHABM is paying a 3-6x premium to the local market and the deck must disclose that.

What does a custom double-wall faceted cup actually cost, and what is the real MOQ and tooling charge? At 40,150 cups/year from one Baghdad unit, SHABM is below every injection-mould MOQ. If the deck's renders show a custom vessel in Year 1, COGS rises USD 0.24-0.50 and Saqee' gross margin falls from 82.8% to 73-78%. This is the single largest unquantified COGS risk in the menu.

Baghdad wholesale FRUIT prices could not be sourced at all — the watermelon (IQD 500-1,000/kg) and strawberry (IQD 2,500-5,000 in season, 8,000-15,000 out) figures are extrapolated from VEGETABLE anchors at Alawa Jamila. The strawberry figure alone drives a 3-4x seasonal COGS swing on the Jana line. Verify in person or at alwaiq.com before the Jana mix is set.

The cafe/dessert industry benchmark ratios (COGS 25-35%, labour 30-35%, prime cost 55-65%, rent 6-10%) are UNSOURCED practitioner knowledge. Re-source from a primary document before an investor sees them — free options are the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, the National Restaurant Association Operations Report, Technomic, or Item 19 of any coffee/dessert franchisor's FDD (available free via the Wisconsin DFI franchise database).

Does SHABM fall inside Iraq's 10% 'deluxe restaurants and hotels' sales tax classification? Iraq has no general VAT, but the assumptions file models a sales_tax scenario at 10% and flags the classification as unresolved. At a 74.5% gross margin this is a ~7.5pp swing in net revenue and it changes every Baghdad price recommendation in this report.

Confirm the Clinebell CB300X2 (or equivalent) price, cycle time and block yield with a factory quote — clinebellequipment.com was blocked. The whole Al-Qalab economics rest on 272 kg per 3.75-day cycle and USD 16,000-24,000 landed, both RECALLED and low confidence. Also confirm whether a second machine can be sourced with a service contract, since the July peak runs one machine at 86% with zero redundancy.

Verify the ULT freezer batch-transfer protocol with a manufacturer. Rated max ambient is 30-32C against a 38-45C Baghdad back-of-house, and the July peak implies a door opening every 2.5 minutes. Ask Thermo/Eppendorf/PHCbi directly whether their unit will hold -80C under that duty cycle in a conditioned 24C room, and what the recovery time per door opening actually is. If the answer is unfavourable, the -80 hero product needs a different freezer architecture entirely.

Egypt: which of the three fixes does management want? (a) enter with a cut menu that drops both Jana boxes and Lafa'if, blending to ~58% net GM; (b) enter at the resort tier (Sharm/Hurghada/El Gouna) at price_index 0.90-0.95 against cost_index 0.62; or (c) make Egypt the network's manufacturing base for the labour-intensive Jana line and not a cafe market at all. The current model books Cairo at -23.1% EBITDA and it never pays back.

Confirm actual observed items-per-ticket and attachment rates once the flagship trades. The entire +23.1% average-ticket recommendation rests on moving items/ticket from 1.42 to 1.83, and 1.42 is itself an assumption in the model, not an observation. This should be the first KPI instrumented in the POS.

Should Al-Qalab be sold by pre-booking or timed release rather than on demand? At the July peak it runs one Clinebell at 86% with a 3.75-day production lead time. A daily released quantity (e.g. 30 vessels, announced) would convert a capacity constraint into a scarcity marketing mechanic — but it needs testing against walk-in conversion.

Verify the exact Ramadan start dates for 2026-2030 against a Hijri calendar authority per country. The recommendation to invert the trading day to 19:00-03:00 during Ramadan is worth an estimated +1.9% annual revenue per unit, and the dates used here were derived from the ~10-11 day lunar drift, not looked up.
